info.title: Midden API
info.description: Everything the Midden web client does goes through this API. See the API guide for authentication, conventions and examples.

get.description: Upgrades to a WebSocket. Send `{"t":"hello","caseId":"...","lastSeq":null}` to join a case, then receive a snapshot and every later operation. The messages are defined by `ClientMessageSchema` and `ServerMessage` in `packages/core/src/sync/protocol.ts`. Read tokens may watch, and any operation they send is rejected.

post.summary: Model Context Protocol endpoint for AI agents
post.description: Speaks JSON-RPC over the stateless form of the Streamable HTTP transport, and takes an API token only, never a session. See the MCP guide.

get.summary: Not supported; this endpoint has no server-sent stream

delete.summary: Not supported; this endpoint has no sessions to end

get.description: The audit trail of every change. Add `format=csv` to download it as a CSV.

post.description: The way to change a case. Send a `clientOpId` so a retry cannot apply twice. Send `baseSeq`, the seq you last saw, to hear in `overwrote` which fields someone else changed since.
Appends a new operation that reverses the old one. Nothing is erased.
Takes nmap XML or normal output. Parsing happens in the background: the scan starts as `parsing`, so poll the list or watch the WebSocket until it is `ready` or `failed`.

get.description: Pass the returned `next` value as `after` to get the next page.

post.summary: Attach a file to an event or host

targetId.description: The id of that event or host.

dangerous.description: Set to `1` to flag the file as dangerous yourself.

get.description: A dangerous file never leaves the server bare. It comes as an encrypted zip with the password `infected`.

delete.description: Tasks keep their team id and show it as a deleted team.

put.summary: Add a member or change their role
put.description: Admins may do anything. A lead of the team may add and remove members, but not leads.

get.summary: List your saved views and those shared with your teams
get.description: Built-in views (My tasks, Everyone’s tasks, …) are part of the web client and not listed.

post.description: Give a `teamId` to share it with a team; only that team’s leads and admins may.

patch.description: Its owner may change a personal view; a lead of the team, a shared one.

get.description: Newest first. Tasks linked to a restricted case are left out unless you can read that case.

get.summary: Every task, comment, run and workflow you can see
A task with its comments and dependencies
get.description: The id may also be a task number: `T-12` or `12`.

patch.description: Moving a task to a done status fails while its approver has not approved it. Changing who is assigned here affects one task, so it needs no lead.

get.description: Operations touching a task you cannot see are left out.

post.description: Takes any client operation from `TaskOpSchema`. Assigning more than one task in one operation takes a team lead or an admin. Send a `clientOpId` so a retry cannot apply twice.
Applies the recorded inverse of that operation as a new one.

post.summary: Start a run (team lead or admin)
post.description: The run gets its own copy of a workflow, so its statuses can change without affecting others.

patch.summary: Rename, move or close a run (team lead or admin)

get.description: Every signed-in user can read playbooks. The CSV itself comes with `GET /api/playbooks/{id}`.

post.summary: Save a playbook (team lead or admin)
post.description: The CSV is checked for errors in the file itself; names of people, teams and cases are only resolved when a run is started from it. A playbook with no team takes an admin.

get.summary: Get a playbook with its CSV

patch.summary: Change a playbook (team lead or admin)

delete.summary: Delete a playbook (team lead or admin)
delete.description: Runs started from it keep their tasks.

post.summary: Save a run as a playbook (team lead or admin)
post.description: Due dates become offsets from the run's start, and by default statuses, ticks and assignees are cleared so the next hunt starts fresh. Case links are dropped, and tasks linked to a restricted case are left out (`skipped`), since a playbook is shared with the whole team.

post.summary: Import tasks from CSV or a playbook (team lead or admin)
post.description: Starts a run (`run`) or adds to one (`runId`), as a single operation that undoes in one step. With `?preview=1` nothing changes: the response lists the tasks as they would be created and every problem found, including the ones the permission checks would raise. Status names the run's workflow lacks are listed in `unknownStatuses`; pass them back in `addStatuses` to add them. See the CSV format in the guide.

get.description: Takes the same filters as `GET /api/tasks` and writes the import format, so an export can be imported again. Cells that start with `= + - @` get a leading `'` so spreadsheets do not run them as formulas; import removes it.

200.description: The tasks in the playbook CSV format.

put.description: The default workflow takes an admin; a run's workflow takes a lead of the run's team. Every task must still have a status in its workflow afterwards.

get.summary: Open work, throughput, cycle time and what is stuck
get.description: Counted over the tasks you can see: a task linked to a restricted case you cannot read is left out of every number. Archived tasks count toward throughput and cycle time but not open work. Give `run` for its burndown.

Off unless the server sets `MIDDEN_METRICS=token`; then it needs an API token belonging to an admin (read-only is enough). Text exposition format 0.0.4. Labels name status categories and teams, never people, cases or tasks. See the metrics guide.

Changes to one task within two minutes fold into one unread notification, and a bulk change is one notification listing every task. Tasks you can no longer see drop out, and a notification left with none is not listed or counted. Page with `before` set to the last `updatedAt`.
Being assigned, @mentioned or asked to approve always notifies you; the grid covers everything else. Your own changes never notify you.

patch.description: Send only what changes; everything else keeps its value.

get.description: Admins see every webhook; team leads see their teams'. `allowedHosts` is the server's MIDDEN_WEBHOOK_ALLOWED_HOSTS: webhooks can only post there, and are off when it is empty.

post.summary: Add a webhook (team lead or admin)
post.description: Posts Rocket.Chat incoming-webhook messages (Slack and Mattermost accept them too). A team's webhook hears about tasks on that team or in its runs; one with no team (admins only) hears about every task. Tasks linked to a restricted case are described by number only.

patch.description: Leave out `url` to keep the current one.

post.description: Waits for the attempt and returns it. A failed test is not retried.

get.description: The last 50, newest first. Failed sends are retried after 30 s, 2 min, 10 min, 30 min and 2 h, then marked failed.

token.description: An API token, sent as `Authorization: Bearer mdn_...`.

session.name: midden_session
session.description: A browser session. Requests that change anything must also send an `X-Midden-Client` header.

prefix.description: The first characters, to recognise the token by.

seq.description: The sequence number of the latest operation.

via.description: The name of the API token that made this change, if one did.

ref.description: The task number as people say it, e.g. `T-12`.

status.description: A status id or name in the task's workflow, or a category such as `todo`.
A status id, name or category.

workflowId.description: Copy this workflow for the run. Defaults to the default workflow.

teamId.description: The team it is shared with; empty for a personal view.
Empty for a playbook every team can use.

statuses.description: Workflow for runs started from it; null uses the default.

version.description: Goes up when the CSV or workflow changes.

teamId.description: Empty for a playbook every team can use (admins only).

statuses.description: Workflow for runs started from it; null uses the default workflow.

keepStatus.description: Keep statuses and ticked checklist items instead of starting fresh.

runId.description: Add the tasks to this run instead of starting one.

run.description: Start this run for the tasks.

startDate.description: ISO-8601; relative due dates count from here. Defaults to now.

addStatuses.description: Statuses to add to the run's workflow, for status names it doesn't have.

line.description: 0 for problems with the file as a whole.

tasks.description: Only tasks you can still see.

grid.description: What happened × how you are related to the task.

queue.description: Tell me about new tasks in my teams' queues.

payload.description: The Rocket.Chat message that was sent.

byCategory.description: Every task that is not archived, open or not, by status category.

unassigned.description: Open, with no one and no team queue.

throughput.description: One entry per week, starting Mondays (UTC).

cycle.description: First in progress to done, for tasks done in the window.

lead.description: Created to done, for tasks done in the window.

teamId.description: Empty for a webhook that hears about every task.

url.description: Masked; the full URL is never returned.
